doc.name: A — non alc spirits catalogue, studio sweep, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: zero-proof aperitif bottle
Category: non alc spirits
Shot programme: studio sweep
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium non alc spirits product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the low-angle monument in a studio sweep treatment.

SUBJECT. A zero-proof aperitif bottle. Lock the product itself to the reference — no proportional drift, no invented branding, no cleaned-up typography. Everything else in the frame is your design decision.

CAMERA. Low angle looking up so the product reads as architecture against the backdrop. Shoot on a 180mm long macro at f/5.6, framing for a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a projected gobo throwing a broken pattern across the background. Stage the product on or against wet river stone, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
